newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening steady after in-line CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening steady after in-line CPI.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open steady in the wake of May U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) data in line with expectations.
The CPI rose 0.1 percent in May. Economists in a Reuter survey had expected a 0.2 percent rise.
Analysts said they did not expect either the CPI or the housing start data to have a big impact on the stock market because they contained few surprises or inflation concerns.
The long bond slipped 10/32, its yield rising to 6.72 percent. The Standard & Poor's September futures contract was down 2.15 to 902.
